# commitclerk

> A command-line tool that writes your git commit messages. It reads the staged diff,
> asks an LLM (OpenAI Chat Completions or the Anthropic Messages API) for a Conventional Commits message, prints it,
> and commits. Implemented as an eleven-module package (`config`, `context`, `diffing`, `deep`,
> `files`, `history`, `gitio`, `trailers`, `prompt`, `providers`, `cli`) that is also built into a single standalone ~2 300-line script,
> `dist/commitclerk.py`, with **zero third-party dependencies** — standard library only
> (`urllib`, `subprocess`, `argparse`), Python 3.8+.
> Installs three identical entry points: `clerk`, `commitclerk`, and `git clerk`.
> Install with `pipx install commitclerk`, or download `dist/commitclerk.py` and run it directly.

MIT licensed community project. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by OpenAI,
Anthropic or GitHub. By default it calls the OpenAI Chat Completions API using the key in
`OPENAI_API_KEY`; `--provider anthropic` calls the Anthropic Messages API with
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

## Features

- **Pre-flight secret scan**: before the first request, every *added* line of the staged diff is checked. Two detectors, not equally trusted. Known credential shapes (`sk-`, `gh[pousr]_`, `github_pat_`, `AKIA`/`ASIA`, `xox[baprs]-`, `AIza`, `-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----`, three-part JWTs) run on every file. A Shannon-entropy heuristic on tokens of 24+ credential-shaped characters is skipped on files classified `generated`, `vendor` and `binary`, where lockfile hashes and minified bundles live, and only fires on a token mixing digits, uppercase and lowercase at 4.0 bits per character or more — which deliberately misses lowercase hex secrets, because they are indistinguishable from the git SHAs and checksums a diff is full of, and firing on every one of those is what gets a scanner switched off. Findings are resolved so the named detector always wins an overlap with the heuristic. A hit refuses the run with **exit 3**, naming file, line and detector and never the match. It runs on the diff *as staged*, before demotion and before the budget, because `--deep` sends each oversized file in full in a call of its own and a scan placed later would clear a payload earlier requests already carried. `--redact` masks each match with `[redacted]` and continues — protecting the request, never the repository, which the notice says. `--no-scan` or `"scan": false` opts out; it is the one setting whose default is on.
- **Zero dependencies**: standard library only; a single readable file you can audit before running it on your source code.
- **Git-native**: also installed as `git-clerk`, so `git add -A && git clerk` works as a git subcommand.
- **Title override**: `-m "<title>"` uses your title verbatim and limits the model to writing the body bullets. The most reliable mode, and the recommended default when the intent isn't obvious from the diff alone.
- **Mixed doc+code detection**: when documentation changes alongside code, the prompt names the documentation files, reports documentation's share of the changed lines, and instructs the model to take the type prefix only from the non-documentation diff lines (so a docstring tweak beside a large changelog entry is `docs:`, while a commit that really implements the documented feature is still `feat:`). The note is placed after the diff, where it is not outweighed by the prose it warns about.
- **Documentation-only detection**: if every staged file is documentation (`.md`, `.mdx`, `.rst`, `.txt`, `.adoc`, anything under `docs/`, or a known name like CHANGELOG / README / ROADMAP / CONTRIBUTING), the prompt switches to a docs-only framing — use the `docs:` prefix and describe the documentation change itself ("record X in the changelog"), never "implement X". This exists because a diff-only generator reading changelog prose about already-shipped work will mislabel a Markdown-only commit as `feat:`, and `git log --grep` plus release tooling then inherit the lie.
- **House-style fingerprint**: before writing, a single `git log -n200 --no-merges` measures what this repository actually does — the Conventional Commits types and scopes in use (or whether prefixes are used at all), whether bodies are bulleted, prose or absent and with which bullet character, the median subject length, the trailer keys, and the subject language when it is unambiguous. The result is a ~600-character "house style" block at the top of the prompt, subtracted from the `--max-chars` diff budget rather than added on top. Fewer than five commits produces no block; the language is named only when one language doubles its runner-up and is supported by a quarter of the subjects. Only counts and shapes are transmitted, never message text — scope names and trailer keys excepted. `--no-house-style` disables it.
- **Worked examples from your own history**: the same `git log -n200` also reports each past commit's touched paths. The two or three whose paths overlap the staged diff most (Jaccard over every path and its parent directories, so a sprawling reformat does not beat a focused fix) are included in the prompt as few-shot examples — subject plus body, body clipped to 400 characters, whole block clipped to 1 400, all of it taken out of the `--max-chars` diff budget. Each is fenced and labelled an earlier commit, preceded by an explicit instruction to copy its voice and never restate its content as work done in this commit. Trailer blocks are stripped, so a borrowed `Co-authored-by:` cannot credit the wrong person. This is the one place past commit message text is transmitted verbatim, so it has a switch of its own: `--no-examples` (or `"examples": false`) drops it and keeps the fingerprint, and `--no-house-style` disables both.
- **Monorepo scope inference**: each staged file is walked up to the nearest ancestor directory holding a workspace manifest (`package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `pom.xml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, `build.gradle`, `build.gradle.kts`, `composer.json`, `Gemfile`, `mix.exs`). When every staged file resolves to the same package, its directory name is offered to the model as the Conventional Commits scope. The nearest manifest wins over the outermost, so a monorepo root `package.json` declaring only `workspaces` never overrides the package a file lives in; the repository root is never a scope, so a single-package repo gets none. Files spanning sibling packages produce an explicit instruction not to scope to one of them. Deferred to the house-style vocabulary: a history with no scopes silences inference entirely, and a scope absent from the history is flagged as new. Only manifest *existence* is checked, never contents; no flag, no configuration, no API call.
- **Conventional Commits**: emits `feat:` / `fix:` / `docs:` / `chore:` / `refactor:` / `test:` / `build:` / `perf:` prefixes; imperative titles under 72 characters; bodies of 2–6 bullets about *why*; no emojis, headers, or code fences.
- **File-class taxonomy**: every staged file is classified as `code`, `test`, `docs`, `generated`, `config`, `vendor` or `binary` (path signals plus the diff's binary markers). The class is attached to each filename in the prompt, with a one-line mix, and the rules take the Conventional Commits type from the classes that are the point of the commit — generated, vendored and binary files are never the subject and their contents are never narrated.
- **Generated files are demoted, not dropped**: a `generated` or `vendor` file's diff body is replaced by `[... generated file, +N -M, contents not shown ...]` beneath its `diff --git` header, before the per-file budget is applied, so the reclaimed characters go to the code files. Bodies under 500 characters are left as-is.
- **Map-reduce for the commits no budget can fit (`--deep`)**: off by default. After demotion, the per-file allocator is asked which files it is about to cut at the current budget; each of those gets one extra request of its own carrying that file's diff in full (capped at 60 000 characters), answered in at most two lines. The answers replace those files' diff bodies as `[summary] ...` lines beneath a `[... file too large to show, +N -M, summarized below ...]` header, and the final call writes the message from those summaries plus the smaller files' real diffs — so the tail of a 5 000-line change is described rather than trimmed away. A note above the diff explains the `[summary]` notation. Cost is N+1 requests where N is the number of oversized files, and zero extra requests when the diff already fits, which is why the flag is safe to set as `"deep": true` in `.clerk.json`. A summary that cannot be obtained is never invented: that file keeps its real body and is trimmed exactly as it would have been, and the failure is named on stderr.
- **Structural facts the diff omits**: `git diff --staged --find-renames --stat --summary` is sent alongside the diff, so renames (with `-M` forced regardless of `diff.renames`), mode changes, creations, deletions and binary file sizes are stated rather than inferred. The summary is capped at 2 000 characters and sits outside the diff budget, so it survives when a large diff is trimmed.
- **Partial-staging note**: if a staged file also has unstaged changes, one line on stderr names it and explains that the message describes the staged version, not the file on disk. Informational only; never blocks.
- **Dry run**: `--dry-run` prints the message and commits nothing.
- **Resilient**: transient failures (`408`, `409`, `429`, `5xx`, `529`) are retried up to twice with exponential backoff and jitter, honouring a numeric `Retry-After`. A refused connection fails immediately. A `400` naming a parameter the tool sent is repaired once (the optional sampling knob is dropped, or renamed when the provider says *"Use 'x' instead"*) and resent; required fields and `model` are never touched. `--timeout` bounds each request.
- **Model agnostic**: any OpenAI Chat Completions model via `--model` or `$OPENAI_MODEL` (default `gpt-4o-mini`). The provider is chosen with `--provider` / `$CLERK_PROVIDER` from an adapter table (URL, headers, payload, response extractor). Three entries: `openai` (Chat Completions, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, default `gpt-4o-mini`), `anthropic` (Messages API, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, default `claude-haiku-4-5`), and `ollama` (local Chat Completions at `http://localhost:11434/v1`, no API key, default `qwen2.5-coder`).
- **Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint**: `--base-url` / `$OPENAI_BASE_URL` points the same adapter at Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp, OpenRouter, Groq, Together or Azure. With a local server the staged diff never leaves the machine.
- **Config file with documented precedence**: every setting resolves through one fixed ladder — command-line flag, then environment variable, then `.clerk.json` at the repository root, then `~/.config/clerk/config.json`, then the built-in default. The project file is meant to be committed, so a team convention stops being flags each person retypes; the user file sets personal defaults across every repository. JSON rather than TOML because `tomllib` needs Python 3.11 and the floor here is 3.8, and a parser of its own would cost the zero-dependency rule. Recognised keys: `provider`, `model`, `base_url`, `timeout`, `max_chars`, `house_style` (`false` is `--no-house-style`), `examples` (`false` is `--no-examples`), `scan` (`false` is `--no-scan`), `deep` (`true` is `--deep`). Discovery starts at `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, not the working directory, so behaviour does not change with the subdirectory you are standing in. API keys are never read from a file. An unknown key is reported on stderr and ignored so a config written for a newer version still works; invalid JSON or a wrongly typed value exits `2` rather than being silently dropped.
- **Author context, the one thing a diff cannot carry**: `--context "<note>"` adds one sentence of intent for this commit, and `.clerk/context.md` at the repository root carries the standing facts (the product's name, which binary the CLI installs as, that `docs/` is internal), read verbatim on every run. Both are strictly additive to the prompt and cannot change what the tool does. They sit after the file list and change summary and before the diff, framed as facts to explain the WHY and explicitly not to be restated as work this commit performed. Both come out of the `--max-chars` diff budget and are truncated at 2 000 characters, the one-off note served first. An unreadable or missing context file is silently empty: a note must never be the reason a commit cannot be written.
- **Ticket trailers from the branch name**: with `ticket_refs` set in a config file, the issue key in the current branch (`feat/PROJ-123-retry-webhooks`) is appended to the finished message as a `Refs: PROJ-123` trailer. The built-in pattern is `[A-Z]{2,10}-\d+|#\d+`, covering Jira, Linear and GitHub; `ticket_pattern` replaces it and turns the feature on by itself. **Off by default** — a `Refs:` trailer on a repository with no tracker is noise. The key is read from `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` and appended after the model has answered, never included in the prompt, so it cannot be paraphrased, dropped or invented. A detached HEAD or a branch with no key produces no trailer; an existing trailer block is joined rather than duplicated, and a `Refs:` already in the message is not repeated.
- **Wrappers**: `run-commit.cmd` (Windows) and `run-commit.sh` (POSIX) check the API key, stage everything with `git add -A`, then pass arguments through. The Python script itself never stages anything.

## Usage

`clerk [-m TITLE] [--context NOTE] [--dry-run] [--provider NAME] [--base-url URL] [--model MODEL] [--timeout S] [--max-chars N] [--deep] [--no-house-style] [--no-examples] [--redact] [--no-scan] [--version]`

- `-m`, `--message TITLE` — use TITLE verbatim as the commit title; the AI writes only the body.
- `--context NOTE` — one sentence of intent the diff cannot show; standing facts belong in `.clerk/context.md`.
- `--dry-run` — print the message and exit without committing.
- `--provider NAME` — provider to call: `openai`, `anthropic`, or `ollama` (default `openai`, or `$CLERK_PROVIDER`). `ollama` needs no API key and calls a local server.
- `--base-url URL` — base URL of an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (default `https://api.openai.com/v1`, or `$OPENAI_BASE_URL`). Must be http:// or https://.
- `--model MODEL` — model to call (default: the provider's default; `gpt-4o-mini` or `$OPENAI_MODEL` for `openai`).
- `--timeout S` — seconds to wait for each API request (default `60`).
- `--max-chars N` — character budget for the diff; a larger diff is trimmed per file so every changed file still reaches the model (default `60000`).
- `--deep` — summarise each file too large for the diff budget in its own request, then write the message from those summaries plus the smaller files' real diffs. One extra request per oversized file; none when the diff already fits.
- `--no-house-style` — skip the `git log` behind both the house-style fingerprint and the worked examples.
- `--no-examples` — send no past commit message text; keep the fingerprint, which is only counts and shapes. Implied by `--no-house-style`.
- `--redact` — mask a suspected secret in the request instead of refusing to send. The commit is unchanged and still contains it.
- `--no-scan` — do not scan the staged diff for secrets before sending it. Turns off `--redact` with it.
- `--version` — print the version and exit.

Every default above can also come from `.clerk.json` at the repository root or
`~/.config/clerk/config.json`; a flag beats an environment variable, which beats the project
file, which beats the user file.

Exit codes: `0` committed (or dry-run printed), `1` nothing staged, `2` configuration problem, `3` the pre-flight scan found a suspected secret and sent nothing
(the provider's API key is not set, the provider does not exist, or a config file cannot be
read as written), anything else passed through from `git commit`.

## Requirements

- Python 3.8+ (no third-party packages)
- `git` on the `PATH`
- An API key in `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with `--provider anthropic` — or no key at all with `--provider ollama` and a local Ollama server

## Privacy and cost

- The staged diff is sent to the configured endpoint (the OpenAI API by default; the Anthropic API with `--provider anthropic`) — on a repository whose contents cannot leave the machine, use `--provider ollama`, which calls a local model and sends nothing over the network, or do not run the tool there. A committed `.clerk.json` can set `base_url` and therefore the destination, so it is a file to read before running the tool in a repository you did not write.
- Nothing else is transmitted, stored, or logged: no telemetry, no analytics, no remote config.
- The API key is read from the environment and never written to disk.
- One API call per commit; a fraction of a cent with either provider's default model.
- `--deep` changes both figures: N+1 calls where N is the number of files too large for the budget, and each of those N carries that file's diff **in full** rather than the trimmed share the budget would have sent. Same endpoint, same key. Off by default for that reason; a commit within budget triggers none of it.
